audit.whatIsWrong: CROSS-LAYER DISAGREEMENT on all seven rows: every phases[N].side reads 'Pantheon' while every content win[N] reads 'Aurora'.
audit.why: Neither layer is wholly right and the prose settles it. whys[0] and whys[1] say outright that Pantheon has the early edge — true from the kit: Comet Spear at 575 and Shield Vault, a point-and-click 600-range stun on 13s, against an Aurora who has no E hop until 3. From level 3 whys[2..6] describe Aurora winning, and they are correct: a spent Shield Vault leaves him 13s with no approach. So rows 0-1 are Pantheon on both layers and rows 2-6 are Aurora on both. Every moved row has its paired edit in this proposal and every why is rewritten to match the verdict above it.
audit.corrected: Pantheon, Pantheon, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..6].why were the stock Aurora spike template under Pantheon-sided rows — the row said one thing and the sentence said the opposite.
audit.why: Every stage has a real Pantheon timer: Q 575 range on 11s, W 600 point-and-click on 13/12/11/10/9, E 22s at rank 1 blocking only the front, R 180/165/150 from 5500 units. The whys now track the side above them.
audit.corrected: All seven rewritten in the same proposal as the side edits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page states that Aegis Assault is an interruptible channel, only that it blocks damage from the front.
audit.why: Riot's text plus the derived channel flag: Aegis Assault is a channel, so Aurora's Between Worlds shockwave — her only hard CC — breaks it, and it is 22s at rank 1. The front-only blocking already on the page is correct and kept. Shield Vault also carries an auto-attack reset, which enemyWin already states.
audit.corrected: Aegis Assault is a channel — your R shockwave breaks it and leaves him 22s of nothing.

audit.why: The packet flags 'Grand Skyfall' in spikes[1].text and 'Comet Spear' in wants.foe[1] as suspect names. Checked against the current text on disk: spikes[1].text already reads Grand Starfall and Comet Spear is Pantheon's real Q. Both are packet false positives — no edit made.

edits.before: Q-poke and recast on his last-hits — the spirit-mark detonation chips harder than the lane expects.
edits.after: Comet Spear at 575 plus a point-and-click 600 stun — hold the 900 Q line and give ground early.

edits.before: W online: the hop + brief stealth is your trade exit and your gank insurance in one button.
edits.after: W online at 2, but it is an exit only — Shield Vault still lands whenever he picks, at 600.

edits.before: E completes the trade loop: the knockback-slow into Q-recast is your bread-and-butter chunk.
edits.after: E at 3 slows him off you the moment the vault lands — he cannot miss it, only spend it.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — three-spell spirit stacks proc your passive haste; trade in full patterns now.
edits.after: Lost Chapter online and his only approach is still Shield Vault on 13s — count it, then trade in full.

edits.before: Between Worlds online — the zone re-prices every fight: enemies inside feed you speed and exits.
edits.after: Between Worlds online — the zone slow holds him outside the 600 units Shield Vault needs.

edits.before: Luden's spike: the full Q-E-Q rotation chunks half bars. Force trades on his cooldown gaps.
edits.after: Luden's spike: the full Q-E-Q rotation chunks half bars. His 22s Aegis Assault covers one side.

edits.before: Late Aurora warps teamfight space: drop R on the objective clump and hop through the panic.
edits.after: Late he is a 150s global engage, not a duellist — hold the 900 line and R the clump he lands in.

edits.before: Carry by never letting him touch you: he has one gap-closer on 13s and nothing at all once it is spent on you.
edits.after: Carry by never letting him touch you: Aegis Assault is a channel — your R shockwave breaks it and leaves him 22s of nothing.

notes: win[2] is proposed with before and after both 'Aurora' purely so the chart group carries its content-layer twin for the row whose side moved to Aurora; if the applier rejects a no-op, the row is already at the correct value on that layer and nothing is lost. Rows 3-6 moved to Aurora on the full layer only because win[3..6] already read Aurora. Rows 0-1 moved to Pantheon on the content layer only because phases[0..1].side already read Pantheon. After this proposal both layers read Pantheon, Pantheon, Aurora x5, which is what the whys and the kit say. Difficulty stays 8/10: Pantheon owning the first two levels and the 600-range stun deciding every step forward is what makes it hard, even though Aurora holds the rows after 3.
